newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says mulls damages suit vs former president.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says mulls damages suit vs former president.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Friday it would consider filing a damages suit against its former president Hideo Sakamaki and two other former executives over the racketeer payoff scandal.

Sakamaki was arrested in May and later indicted on charges of violating the Commercial Code and the Securities and Exchange Law. He is accused of conspiring with other Nomura executives to pay 49.73 million yen to "sokaiya" corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike between January 31 and June 15, 1995.

Asked at its annual shareholders' meeting on Friday if the company would seek seek damages against Sakamaki, Nomura said it may take such action if the accusations are proved, according to information issued by the company on its website.
Nomura is providing a written summary of a question-and-answer session at its shareholders' meeting on the Internet in a move to increase transparency in the wake of the payoff scandal.
The summary said Sakamaki and two other former executives have been indicted in the case, and if the charges are proved it would consider the course of action suggested by the questioner.
Prosecutors have also served a further arrest warrant on Sakamaki and the ex-Nomura executives on suspicion of paying 320 million yen to Koike sometime around March 24, 1995.

Sakamaki was suspected of conspiring with the two others to give the money to Koike in exchange for a pledge by him to ensure the smooth running of its shareholders' meeting that was held on June 29, 1995.
Prosecutors allege that the money was given directly to Koike in cash at Nomura's headquarters, in violation of Japanese law.
